titel: Still guessing joint clearance? Print this first 🧪 | Blender

eind.zin: Find your gap first, then cut the joints in your figure.

printzin: Measured in Blender, not print tested by us yet.

scenes.tekst: Before you print a whole figure, print this small fit test strip first.
scenes.label: TIP

scenes.tekst: In Click Joints Pro, press Fit test: ball, or Fit test: hinge.
scenes.label: ONE BUTTON

scenes.tekst: You get five ball joints, from 0.10 to 0.30 mm clearance.
scenes.uitspraak: You get five ball joints, from zero point one to zero point three millimetres clearance.
scenes.label: FIVE JOINTS

scenes.tekst: Each joint has its clearance number on top, so you know which one is which.
scenes.label: NUMBERED

scenes.tekst: The hinge strip works the same way, for knees and elbows.
scenes.label: HINGES TOO

scenes.tekst: Print both strips, try each joint, and pick the gap that fits your printer.
scenes.label: PICK YOUR GAP

scenes.tekst: Set that clearance before you cut your figure. The default is 0.2 mm.
scenes.uitspraak: Set that clearance before you cut your figure. The default is zero point two millimetres.
scenes.label: USE IT

scenes.tekst: Measured in Blender, not print tested by us yet. Every printer is different.
scenes.label: HONEST

scenes.tekst: Click Joints Pro. Find your gap first, then print the figure.
scenes.label: CLICK JOINTS PRO
